entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__form_input
entries.description: Set values in form elements using element reference ID from the read_page tool. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

tabId.description: Tab ID to set form value in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_network_requests
entries.description: Read HTTP network requests (XHR, Fetch, documents, images, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging API calls, monitoring network activity, or understanding what requests a page is making. Returns all network requests made by the current page, including cross-origin requests. Requests are automatically cleared when the page navigates to a different domain. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read network requests from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

urlPattern.description: Optional URL pattern to filter requests. Only requests whose URL as listed (auth values shown as REDACTED) contains this string will be returned (e.g., '/api/' to filter API calls, 'example.com' to filter by domain).

clear.description: If true, clear the network requests after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

### sopa_panela
A large brushed-steel stockpot of thick, chunky vegetable soup simmering on a gas stove in a modest home kitchen. Overhead top-down shot with a slow, continuous push-in. The entire pot is visible and fills most of the frame: carrots, potatoes, pumpkin, beans, leafy greens and short pasta are spread evenly through a golden broth, small bubbles rise and burst, soft steam drifts across the lens. Morning window light from one side puts warm highlights on the steel rim. The pot reads as one complete, well-mixed whole.

### sopa_concha_mergulha
Close-up at the height of the pot rim: a hand holding a stainless steel ladle slowly dips it into a large pot of thick vegetable soup, sinks it deep, gives one slow stir and lifts it out full. The camera rises with the ladle in slow motion, broth dripping from its edge; the scoop holds a balanced mix of carrots, potatoes, beans, pumpkin and broth, a small faithful portrait of the whole pot. Steam backlit by window light. Only the hand and forearm are visible.

### sopa_concha_pobre
Close-up in the same home kitchen, over the same large pot of thick vegetable soup. A hand lifts a stainless steel ladle out of the pot in slow motion, and the ladle comes up holding almost only thin, clear broth with two or three tiny pieces of vegetable floating in it, plainly unrepresentative of the chunky soup below, where carrots, potatoes and beans remain clearly visible. The camera holds on the nearly empty ladle while broth drips back into the pot. Side window light, rising steam. Only the hand is visible.

### sopa_concha_rica
Close-up in the same home kitchen, over the same large pot of vegetable soup. A hand lifts a stainless steel ladle in slow motion and it comes up overloaded: chunks of carrot, potato, pumpkin and beans piled high above the rim with almost no broth, a few pieces tumbling back into the pot. The overflowing scoop clearly misrepresents the mostly liquid soup beneath it. The camera holds at ladle height, steam backlit by window light. Only the hand is visible.

input.command:
cat > REDACTED.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/zsh
set -e
cd /Users/leonardodias/arvor/PNAD/video/masterclass
OUT=midia/entrada; TMP=midia/brutos; mkdir -p $OUT $TMP
BIN=~/anaconda3/envs/diffusionkit/bin/mflux-generate-flux2
export PATH="$PATH:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin"
python3 - <<'PY' > /tmp/stills2_prompts.tsv
import json
m=json.load(open('midia/manifesto.json'))
quero=['boletim_impressora','sopa_mesa','escola_bangu_aerea','rio_amazonia_escola','cedulas_argentina_abstrato','fiscal_cadeira']
for i in m['itens']:
    if i['id'] in quero:
        print(i['id']+'\t'+'Still photograph. '+i['prompt'].replace('\n',' ')+' Avoid: '+i.get('negativo',''))
PY
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id prompt; do
  [ -f $OUT/${id}_16x9.mp4 ] && continue
  echo "== $id"
  $BIN --model flux2-klein-9b --prompt "$prompt" --height 1088 --width 1920 --steps 4 --quantize 8 --seed 2026 --output $TMP/${id}_still.png
  # Ken Burns: 8 s, zoom lento 1.0 -> 1.12 com leve deriva
  ffmpeg -v error -y -loop 1 -i $TMP/${id}_still.png -vf "scale=2304:1306,zoompan=z='1+0.12*on/240':x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)+20*on/240':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)':d=240:s=1920x1080:fps=30,format=yuv420p" -t 8 -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -movflags +faststart -an $OUT/${id}_16x9.mp4
done < /tmp/stills2_prompts.tsv
echo STILLS2_DONE
EOF
chmod +x REDACTED.sh && REDACTED.sh > /Users/leonardodias/arvor/PNAD/video/masterclass/out_stills2.log 2>&1

Vídeo de 14:41 em 16:9 e 9:16 (`video/masterclass/`, Remotion 4, cópia generalizada de `video/fiscais/`, que segue intacto). Contrato entre as peças em `video/masterclass/CONTRATO.md`; sete capítulos e 37 cenas em `src/ordem.ts`; registro de cenas em `src/cenas/registro.ts` (capítulos 0 a 2) e `registro_b.ts` (3 a 6), com `satisfies Record<CenaId, CenaDef>` para o typecheck reprovar cena sem componente. Reprodução, nesta ordem: `python3 scripts/video-masterclass-dados.py` (grava `src/dados/masterclass.json`, nada digitado à mão), roteiro em `roteiro/roteiro.md` (fontes em `roteiro/fontes.md`), `python3 scripts/video-masterclass-voz.py` (narração v4 e efeitos; sem `--sem-musica` gera uma faixa por capítulo pelo `/v1/music`, com duração igual à extensão do capítulo + 12 s), `python3 scripts/video-masterclass-midia.py` (clipes e stills), `python3 scripts/video-masterclass-capturas.py` (gravações Playwright das páginas), `npm run verificar` (portão 840 a 930 s; 13 minutos é proibido), `node stills.mjs`, `npm run render`. Teste: `pytest -q tests/test_video_masterclass.py`.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
entries.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one.

repository.description: With target "cloud", only when the user named a repository other than this project's: "owner/name" on github.com, which the cloud session clones at its default branch. Take the exact owner/name from the user's words or a listing that shows it; if you are not sure of it, ask them. A bypass or auto permission mode may not carry over: the session then starts in the cloud's default mode. If the call is refused, do not run or propose the other repository's work in this project.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

# Repository Guidelines

## Canonical Workspace
- The only writable source of truth for this project is `~/arvor/PNAD`.
- `~/clawd/projects/PNAD` is a replicated vault mirror. Treat it as read-only: never create, edit, generate, copy, or retain project artifacts there.
- Project reports, sources, datasets, scripts, tests, images, and temporary work must stay under `~/arvor/PNAD`.

## Single Source of Truth
- Agent instructions live in `AGENTS.md`.
- `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` should be symlinks to this file.

## Project Structure & Module Organization
- Runtime data layout (local, heavy files ignored):
  - `data/raw/`: PNADC trimestral `.zip` / `.txt`.
  - `data/raw/pnadc_anual_visita1/`: PNADC anual visita 1.
  - `data/raw/pnadc_anual_visita5/`: PNADC anual visita 5.
  - `data/raw/tse_eleitorado/`: pacotes de perfil do eleitorado (TSE), incluindo `perfil_eleitorado_ATUAL.zip`.
  - `data/originals/`: IBGE docs/layouts + `salario_minimo.csv`.
  - `data/originals/pnadc_anual_visita1/`: documentacao anual visita 1.
  - `data/originals/pnadc_anual_visita5/`: documentacao anual visita 5.
  - `data/originals/censo_2022_renda_responsavel/`: agregados do Censo 2022 (renda do responsavel).
  - `data/outputs/`: `base*.csv`, `ipca.csv`, `brasil.sqlite`, `tse_eleitorado_perfil.sqlite`, `tse_eleitorado_perfil_summary.csv`, `tse_eleitorado_perfil_benchmark.json`.
- Root docs/metadata:
  - `README.md`: usage and operational docs.
  - `AGENTS.md`: repository guidance.
- Published site (`docs/`, served by GitHub Pages at `brasil.arvor.co`):
  - `docs/index.html`: hand-written library hub linking every report. Not generated; edit directly.
  - `docs/pnad.html`: interactive PNADC essay, generated by `python docs/build_index.py` from `docs/index.template.html`.
  - `docs/<instituto>_<data>.html`: poll audit dossiers, plus `_thread.html` / `_slides.html` companions.
- Code and analysis:
  - `scripts/` for Python CLI/utilities.
  - `notebooks/` for exploratory analyses.
  - `tests/` for `pytest` automated tests.
- `skills/` for project-local agent skills (e.g., `skills/brasil-cli-analyst/SKILL.md`).
  - `data/` scaffold only (`.gitkeep`).

## Core Commands
- Inspect raw file: `head -n 20 data/raw/PNADC_032025.txt`
- Validate size: `wc -l data/raw/PNADC_032025.txt`
- Run tests: `pytest -q`
- Main CLI help: `python scripts/pnad.py --help`
- Legacy command help: `python scripts/pnad.py help-legacy`
- Inspect TSE electorate profile summary: `sqlite3 data/outputs/tse_eleitorado_perfil.sqlite "SELECT * FROM atlas_comparison"`
- Inspect TSE electorate profile metadata: `sqlite3 data/outputs/tse_eleitorado_perfil.sqlite "SELECT * FROM metadata"`
- Rebuild TSE compact profile: `python3 scripts/tse-electorate-profile.py`

## Installable CLI (`brasil`)
- Install locally: `pip install -e .`
- Compatibility alias: `pnad` remains available for legacy scripts.
- Then use directly:
  - `brasil --help`
  - `brasil ibge-sync`
  - `brasil ibge-sync --full`
  - `brasil pipeline-run --raw latest`
  - `brasil query --db data/outputs/brasil.sqlite --sql "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'"`
  - `brasil renda-por-faixa-sm --input data/outputs/base_labeled.csv --group-by pais`
  - `brasil dashboard --input data/outputs/base_labeled.csv --interactive`

## Pipeline Defaults
- Pipeline command: `brasil pipeline-run`
- Steps executed:
  - emit code tables (`emit-codes`)
  - fixed-width extraction (`fwf-extract`)
  - code label join (`join-codes`)
  - IPCA refresh (`fetch_ipca.py`)
  - NPV adjustment (`npv_deflators.py apply`)
  - SQLite build (optional, on by default in pipeline)
- Outputs in `data/outputs/`:
  - `base.csv`, `base_labeled.csv`, `base_labeled_npv.csv`
  - `ipca.csv`
  - `brasil.sqlite` (table `base_labeled_npv`)
- Automatic defaults in `pipeline-run`:
  - If `--target` is omitted, use latest month from `--ipca-csv`.
  - If `--min-wage` is omitted, resolve from `--salario-minimo-csv` at or before target.
  - Manifest includes `target`, `min_wage`, `min_wage_source_month`.

## Key Data Variables
- TSE electorate profile:
  - Raw source: `data/raw/tse_eleitorado/perfil_eleitorado_ATUAL.zip`.
  - Summary DB: `data/outputs/tse_eleitorado_perfil.sqlite`.
  - Summary CSV: `data/outputs/tse_eleitorado_perfil_summary.csv`.
  - Tables: `metadata`, `summary`, `atlas_comparison`.
  - Useful summary dimensions: `genero_atlas_binario`, `idade_atlas`, `regiao`, `uf`, `cor_raca`, `escolaridade_tse`.
- Income:
  - `VD4019__rendim_habitual_qq_trabalho`
  - `VD4020__rendim_efetivo_qq_trabalho`
  - NPV-adjusted suffix: `_<YYYYMM>`
  - Minimum-wage suffix: `_mw`
  - Replicate weights for sampling uncertainty: `V1028001..V1028200`
- Geography:
  - `UF__unidade_da_federacao`, `Capital__municipio_da_capital`, `RM_RIDE__reg_metr_e_reg_adm_int_des`
- Household:
  - `dom_id` composed from `Ano`, `Trimestre`, `UPA`, `V1008`

## Income Methodology
- Bands: `0-2`, `2-5`, `5-10`, `10+` minimum wages.
- Minimum wage source: `data/originals/salario_minimo.csv` (updated by `brasil ibge-sync`).
- Deflator: IPCA monthly index to target month (default = latest month in series).
- Per-capita income: household total divided by `VD2003__nmero_de_componentes_do_domic`.
- Weighted estimation default:
  - Use `V1028` (fallback `V1027`) for population distribution.
  - `--unweighted` is diagnostic only (not official estimate).

## Electorate Profile Methodology
- For electoral polling audits, use TSE electorate data to complement PNAD.
- Use TSE for age, sex/gender, UF and macro-region because the target universe is the electorate.
- Use PNAD for income and schooling when auditing social composition:
  - TSE has no income.
  - TSE schooling is cadastro-based and can be stale when voters do not update education after registration.
- Treat TSE race/color cautiously. In the current `perfil_eleitorado_ATUAL.zip`, `DS_COR_RACA` has very high `Nao informado`; do not use it as a strong calibration target without checking missingness.
- For national comparisons, exclude `SG_UF='ZZ'` (exterior) unless the poll universe includes voters abroad.
- Do not extract huge TSE CSVs to disk by default. Process the ZIP in streaming mode and persist compact summaries in SQLite/CSV.

## Previsão presidencial experimental (03/10/2026)
- `python3 scripts/predicao-2026-build.py --refresh-agregador --hoje 2026-10-04` atualiza a previsão e o card após integrar pesquisas. Fonte: `docs/predicao_2026_1T_presidente.template.html` e `scripts/predicao_2026/`; nunca editar a página gerada diretamente.
- Preparar dados oficiais com `predicao-2026-fontes.py`, `predicao-2026-tse.py` e `predicao-2026-validar.py`. Usar eleitorado federal final de 2026; registrar datas, hashes e diferenças de totais. Snapshots preservam cada versão.
- A retrospectiva 2018→2022 não favoreceu o modelo por seção (RMSE ponderado 1,24 contra 1,19 pp da UF). Central estadual; seções para diagnóstico e cenários. Valida apenas comparecimento, não preferências ou probabilidades de vitória.
- Efeitos de casa são diferenças relativas a pares contemporâneos, não erros eleitorais identificados. PNAD e voto útil extra são hipóteses explícitas. Preservar eleitorado = válidos + brancos/nulos + abstenção e paridade Python/navegador. Nunca inferir voto dos ausentes pelo endereço da seção.

- Recência da previsão: meia-vida nacional 3 dias e estadual 7 dias pelo ponto médio do campo; uma onda por casa/UF, com campo mais recente prioritário. CLI permite ajustar ambas. Central inclusiva usa PNAD onde há cruzamento e publicada onde falta; nunca imputar renda ausente. Agregador descritivo continua com peso igual. Transcrições estaduais novas em `analysis/predicao_2026/estaduais/`, com páginas e hashes da fonte.
- Para cruzamentos Quaest recentes, `predicao-2026-estaduais.py` guarda conferência visual e OCR. Recomposição admite ±0,5 pp por número inteiro e preferência livre do NS/NR de hábito; envelope aritmético não é IC. Selecionar os que pretendem votar dentro do grupo irregular assume o voto do grupo agregado, pois o subconjunto não é publicado. Expor resíduos, cobertura e alternativa sem seleção; não carregar sinal de onda anterior como atual.

## Previsão presidencial, segunda versão (03/10/2026, véspera da eleição)
- A página ganhou mapa interativo (`scripts/predicao_2026/mapa.py`, `docs/assets/predicao_2026_mapa.js` e `.css`), simulador com cenários prontos e link compartilhável (`scripts/predicao_2026/simulador.py`, parte DOM de `docs/assets/predicao_2026.js`; fragmento `#sim=vf:50;rNE:-5;SP:cp2,vf60`), âncora dinâmica e validação preditiva (`scripts/predicao_2026/dinamico.py` e `preditiva.py`). Contrato entre simulador e mapa: evento `predicao:cenario` em `document`, com `{result, params, central}`, e cópia em `window.predicaoCenario`.
- **Machine learning supervisionado não é treinável aqui**: o acervo tem uma eleição de referência (2022, mais 2018 só para comparecimento), as pesquisas finais de 2022 arquivadas desde 03/10 e nenhuma de 2018. Treinar pesquisa→urna com um ponto é ajustar ruído. A avaliação completa está em `analysis/predicao_2026/avaliacao_ml.md`. O caminho defensável é o modelo dinâmico bayesiano de espaço de estados (Jackman 2005; Linzer 2013; Heidemanns, Gelman e Morris 2020), com efeitos de casa, passeio aleatório e pooling parcial estadual, que é o que o motor já faz em parte.
- **Âncora dinâmica (DLM)**: nível local nas cinco categorias, efeitos de casa de soma zero, variâncias por máxima verossimilhança com filtro de Kalman, multiplicador de erro não amostral phi estimado em 2,10 (deff efetivo 3,15; phi = 1 rejeitado por razão de verossimilhança). Entra no simulador e nas sensibilidades, não na central: nos válidos dá Lula 44,21 × Flávio 42,63 contra 44,0 × 43,0 da central.
- **Validação preditiva de origem móvel** (prevê as pesquisas seguintes, nunca a urna; origens 01/09 a 01/10, horizonte 1 a 7 dias, 204 pares): a central (recência 3 dias, janela 7) tem MAE 3,43 pp na diferença L−F; o DLM, 3,53; pareado por onda a diferença é +0,10 com erro-padrão 0,14. Nenhuma meia-vida ou janela se separa da central. Todas as âncoras tiveram viés positivo em setembro: as ondas seguintes vieram menos favoráveis a Lula, e âncora sem termo de deriva não antecipa tendência. Efeitos de casa servem para prever a próxima onda da mesma casa (MAE 2,07 contra 3,19 da central), não o nível do país.
- **Central desde 03/10 à noite = recência + tendência encolhida + indecisos por disponibilidade.** `DEFAULTS["base"] = "central_inclinacao"` em `motor.py` e no espelho JS: a média por recência (inclusivo) deslocada pelas inclinações de 28 dias da regressão de efeito fixo de casa, cada uma encolhida por b² / (b² + ep²), projetada da data efetiva da média até 04/10 (`base.sloped_central`). O destino central dos indecisos é a disponibilidade (1 − rejeição, `rejeicao.py`), resolvida para número no build e gravada em `central.parametros`; `DEFAULTS["indecisos_flavio"]` continua `None`, e o simulador (link, frase, detector de central) compara com `central.parametros`, nunca com os defaults crus. Proporcional vira `if:p` no link.
- Critério declarado antes do teste (origem móvel, horizonte 1 a 3 dias): MAE pareado não pior e viés menor em módulo. Central + inclinação passou (MAE 3,04 contra 3,16, pareado −0,12 com ep 0,15; viés +0,42 contra +1,17); o DLM com tendência reprovou (3,41, viés +1,63). Ganho modesto, não significativo, escolhido entre quatro variantes; validação contra pesquisas, não contra a urna. Os números da página saem do JSON por `texto.trend_values` e `texto.learning_values`.
- Monte Carlo (`motor.simulate` e `Prediction2026.simulate`): toda âncora calculada sobre as casas centrais reutiliza o bootstrap delas recentrado por `alvos[base] − alvos.inclusivo` (`motor.bootstrap_design`); a incerteza da projeção (`nacional.incerteza_projecao_pp`: horizonte × dp(β_F − β_L) para a central, √(dp_proj² − dp_corte²) para a tendência do DLM) soma-se em quadratura ao erro comum de 2 pp; o destino dos indecisos central entra nos sorteios. Documentado em `configuracao.incerteza`.
- **Consolidação sem dupla contagem**: os presets e sensibilidades de consolidação (proporção medida e disponibilidade) partem de `base: "inclusivo"`, porque a central já projeta a queda da terceira via; `consolidacao.anchor_start` usa a data efetiva da âncora inclusivo. `consolidacao.comparacao_central` registra que central e consolidação de 28 dias ficam a centésimos e por quê.
- **Erro das pesquisas de 2022** (`python3 scripts/predicao-2026-erro-2022.py` grava `analysis/predicao_2026/erro_2022/erro_2022.json`; memorando ao lado; documentos e `fonte.json` com SHA-256 em `data/originals/pesquisas_2022/<casa>/`, no LFS e no `git lfs pull` do CI). O build copia o bloco para `erro_2022` do payload (`scripts/predicao_2026/erro_2022.py`) e a seção 06 o publica por `view.erro_2022_table`, `view.erro_2022_vs_2026` e `texto.error_2022_values`, com o desvio relativo de 2026 relido do build corrente.
- Números de 2022 (12 casas): erro comum na diferença L−B +3,92 pp dos válidos (mediana +4,96), Lula −0,42, Bolsonaro −4,33; dispersão entre casas 4,96, maior que o erro comum; piores Datafolha, Ipec e Ipespe (+8,77, citar as três), melhor Paraná Pesquisas (+1,87); sinal estável e tamanho de +1,96 a +5,03 conforme a regra de inclusão.
- Regra de uso: medição histórica e cenário nas duas direções (sensibilidades `vies_pp = ±erro comum`, lido do JSON), nunca prognóstico nem ajuste da central; o desvio de 2 pp do erro comum continua parâmetro declarado e 2022 é referência de magnitude. Falta 2018: arquivar as últimas ondas nacionais com URL, SHA-256 e página, transcrever no formato de `pesquisas_2022.json` e rodar a mesma conta; ainda assim seriam dois pontos.
- `tests/conftest.py` coloca `scripts/` no caminho de importação; testes novos importam no topo, sem `sys.path` nem `noqa`. Lint zero agora inclui `tests/`.
- Snapshots: cada build com código alterado grava um snapshot novo; ao fechar uma rodada, manter só o snapshot do hash publicado.
- CNT/MDA 171ª rodada (03/10/2026, `analysis/reponderacao/pesquisas/mda_2026-10-02.json`, PDF em `data/originals/mda_102026_03/`): a íntegra sai no upload público da CNN (`admin.cnnbrasil.com.br/wp-content/uploads/sites/12/AAAA/MM/Relatorio-Pesquisa-CNT-de-Opiniao-R<rodada>-<MES><AA>.pdf`); o site da CNT e o Poder360 não a tinham na hora. Os cruzamentos são imagem: ler na renderização a 130 dpi com recorte ampliado dos rótulos da borda direita e recompor o placar por renda e por sexo antes de usar. A p. 2 passou a declarar ponderação por escolaridade e renda. Em `cdn.cnt.org.br/diretorioVirtualPrd/` há relatórios antigos (rodada 151, fev/2022): pista para arquivar as pesquisas de 2022 que a calibração do erro comum exige.

## Centrais do segundo turno (09/10/2026)

## Coding Style & Naming
- Prefer Python (PEP 8, 4 spaces).
- Script naming: `kebab-case` (new files), keep existing names for compatibility.
- Keep scripts stream-first for large data; avoid loading full files in memory when not needed.

## Testing Guidelines
- Tests in `tests/`, names `test_*.py`.
- Cover parsing, type conversion, schema checks, and CLI behavior.
- Run `pytest -q` before merging.
- CI precisa de `fetch-depth: 0` para conferir as datas do sitemap. As malhas compactas de `apuracao/public/geo/` e `data/originals/ibge_malhas/br_uf/br_uf_minima.geojson` são dependências versionadas da renderização, não caches descartáveis.
- Comparações com `apuracao/data/secoes_2026.sqlite` exigem o banco local pesado e são condicionais; os contratos dos fragmentos públicos continuam testados sem ele. A exportação Excel exige `openpyxl` em `requirements.txt`.

## Commit & PR Guidelines
- Commit style: imperative + scoped (example: `add brasil pipeline-run sqlite refresh`).
- PR should include:
  - purpose and change summary
  - commands used for validation
  - backward-compat notes (schema/column changes)

## Security & Data Handling
- Avoid committing sensitive or proprietary data.
- Prefer lightweight samples in `samples/` for tests.
- Normalize line endings to LF.
- Use Git LFS for large binaries when needed.

## Lessons Learned
- Safe filtering uses restricted AST compilation (`pnadc_cli.RowExpr`).
- Delimiter/header detection uses `parse_pnadc.sniff_delimiter` with fallbacks.
- SAS layout parser (`layout_sas.parse_layout`) supports labels/slugs and stable ordering.
- Official IBGE layout files (`data/originals/input_PNADC_trimestral.sas` and `.txt`) are `ISO-8859-1` (`latin-1`), not UTF-8.
- Reading layout in wrong encoding introduces mojibake in labels/slugs (example: `federacao`/`primria` artifacts); keep layout parsing encoding-aware and keep generated CSV/JSON output in UTF-8.
- If mojibake appears in derived headers/labels, rerun extraction pipeline after fixing layout encoding handling.
- `fwf-extract` can derive `data_nascimento` and `dom_id`.
- `household-agg` streams rows and aggregates by `dom_id`.
- `npv_deflators.py` applies deflators and minimum-wage conversion in streaming mode.
- `brasil ibge-sync` refreshes monthly minimum wage from BCB SGS series `1619`.
- `brasil pipeline-run --raw latest` auto-resolves `target` (latest IPCA month) and `min_wage` from `salario_minimo.csv`.
- `brasil renda-por-faixa-sm` and `brasil dashboard` default to weighted population estimates (`V1028`, fallback `V1027`).
- `brasil renda-por-faixa-sm` and `brasil dashboard` now compute sampling margin of error/CI by default (bootstrap replicate weights, `V1028001..V1028200`) when replicate columns are present.
- CI controls: `--no-ci` to disable, `--ci-level` to change confidence level.
- If legacy CSVs were generated before replicate columns were included, CI falls back to disabled until pipeline is rerun.
- `brasil dashboard` default `--sm-mode` is `alvo`; use `--sm-mode both` for period-vs-target comparison.
- `DEFAULT_KEEP` in `fwf-extract` now includes additional high-value modeling fields (sampling, schooling, labor-force and job-formality variables) with good observed coverage in PNADC 2025Q3 profiling.
- `DEFAULT_KEEP` also includes all 200 replicate weights to support uncertainty estimation end-to-end in open workflows.
- Terminal output now has high-contrast Brazilian palette by faixa:
  - green (mais pobre), yellow (media baixa), blue (media alta), white (mais rica).
- `--group-by uf` default ordering is `renda_desc` (richer to poorer by average household SM).
- Dashboard sections now include:
  - top 10 UFs by income and by population,
  - macro-region panel,
  - socioeconomic "thermometer" insights (richest/poorest UF and concentration in lowest/highest faixa).
- Pretty outputs now map faixa de SM to BRL ranges (`R$`) for direct interpretation.
- Dashboard now includes an age pyramid (sexo x idade) and age recuts ordered by age buckets.
- For restricted-universe variables, dashboard labels non-response explicitly:
  - `Nao se aplica (fora da ocupacao)` for occupation-only variables,
  - `Fora de RM/RIDE` for metro-region variable,
  avoiding false inflation of `Sem informacao`.
- `brasil query` is optimized for LLM workflows:
  - default output is JSON,
  - read-only SQL is enforced by default,
  - supports SQL via `--sql`, `--sql-file`, or stdin pipe,
  - table rendering is available via `--format table`,
  - JSON includes `sampling` metadata; CI is not auto-derived for arbitrary SQL.
- In PNADC layout, `var. auxil.` means `variavel auxiliar` (roteamento do questionario), not necessarily `auxilio social`.
- For labor income decomposition, keep `V4033/V4034*` (trabalho principal) together with `V405*` (trabalho secundario/outros); omitting `V403*` undercounts detailed components.

- `brasil ibge-sync --full` sincroniza escopos eleitorais completos: PNADC trimestral + PNADC anual visita 5 + Censo 2022 (renda do responsavel) + TSE (perfil do eleitorado).

- The territorial annex is **not** public before fieldwork. Res. TSE 23.600, art. 2º, §7º lets the institute file the municipality and neighbourhood list from the divulgation day up to the next day, and the July 2026 Datafolha registration says so in its own words. What is public at registration time is metadata: field dates, sample size, contractor, value, questionnaire and a generic sampling plan. Do not claim the map leaks before the field; that claim was published once and corrected.
- The predictability comes from repetition, not from the filing deadline: June's annex, public since 19/06, already contained 137 of July's 139 municipalities. The auditable consequence of the current rule is different and sharper: because the annex only arrives after divulgation, **there is no public proof that the sample was defined before the field**. That is what the hashed prior deposit (Res. § 7º-X, PL § 12-A) fixes.
- Rebuild the June–July 2026 Quaest territorial comparison with `python3 scripts/quaest-territory-audit.py --refresh-ibge`. It validates selected sectors against the Panorama service and writes auditable CSV/JSON without imputing vote from Census demographics.
- Rebuild the Atlas July/2026 numbers with `python3 scripts/atlas-072026-audit.py` (writes `docs/assets/atlas_072026_audit.json`) and the Datafolha territorial concentration with `python3 scripts/datafolha-072026-cidades.py` (writes `docs/assets/datafolha_072026_territorio.json`). The second reads the CSV produced by `datafolha-072026-audit.py`, so it needs no `pdfplumber`.
- Atlas crossbreaks are published as images inside the PDF; `pdftotext` and PyMuPDF return only titles. Render the crossbreak pages (`fitz` at ~115 dpi) and transcribe them into the audit script's constant tables, citing the page number.
- When a poll asks both the current-year vote and a "repeat the last election" scenario, the difference between the two isolates the succession cost inside one sample — same respondents, same weights, same recruitment bias. In Atlas 07/2026 it yields Jair 42.3 × Flávio 35.8, with the loss concentrated in the non-bolsonarista right (−20.3) and the unaligned (−19.7), not in the hard base (−2.5). Publish it as descriptive: Atlas gives no unweighted bases, so the gap gets no confidence interval.
- Cross the fear question with the vote question per segment to get the conversion gap — how much emotional advantage a candidate holds and has not converted. Positive gaps mark a trust deficit, not an opinion deficit.
- Datafolha's national design is a fixed master sample: 139 municipalities, 118 identical across May–July 2026, 87.4% of July interviews inside them, only two city swaps between June and July, and AP/RR absent in all waves. Sector rotation, by contrast, jumped from 23% to 79% new between the two intervals. Fixed PSUs are legitimate and reduce the variance of change; the auditable problem is the unpublished selection probability, strata, rotation rule and design effect.
- With ~6 interviews per census sector, Kish's `deff = 1 + (m − 1)ρ` means `ρ = 0.088` erases the 5-point second-round lead and `ρ = 0.736` would be needed to erase the 8-point first-round lead. Report both directions: the first round survives, the second does not.
- Web illustrations for dossiers must come from free-licensed sources (Wikimedia Commons) with author and licence credited in the sources section. Wikimedia rejects arbitrary thumbnail widths — request 800/1280/2560 px or fetch the original via the API.
- Reveal-on-scroll must be gated behind a `js` class added inline in `<head>`, so a page whose script fails still renders every section.
- Rebuild the Atlas income re-weighting with `python3 scripts/atlas-072026-renda.py` (writes `docs/assets/atlas_072026_renda.json`). It streams `base_anual_labeled_npv.csv` (PNADC anual 2024, visita 5) and `base_anual_visita1_labeled_npv.csv` (PNADC anual 2025, visita 1), both already present in `data/outputs/`.
- Poll income quotas are stated in **nominal** reais, so the vintage of the reference PNAD is itself an auditable choice. Atlas 07/2026 declares PNADC 2024 while PNADC anual 2025 had been published in May/2026. Expressing the *same* 2024 microdata at April/2026 prices already moves the R$2.000–3.000 band from 17.3% to 11.9%, because two minimum wages crossed the R$3.000 ceiling (R$2,824 in 2024, R$3,036 in 2025, R$3,242 in 2026) and 42% of that band sat between R$2,700 and R$3,000.
- Re-weighting a published topline on a single margin is legitimate as sensitivity analysis when the published margin reproduces the topline (Atlas 07/2026 does, to 0.1 pp). Always label it as such: the institute's weighting is joint and unpublished. Prefer the same-vintage/price-corrected line as the headline claim, because it is immune to the visita 1 × visita 5 composition objection.
- Never compare two polls on raw percentages when their non-choice shares differ: Atlas 07/2026 has 1.6% blank+null+don't-know against Datafolha's 11%, and those 9.4 points mechanically compress every candidate share in one of them. On **valid votes** the same two polls agree to 0.99 on both Lula and Flávio, and diverge only on movement candidacies — Renan Santos 2.30x, Samara Martins (UP) 1.86x, against Caiado 0.69x, Cury 0.71x and Zema 0.83x. The right/left symmetry is what makes the finding immune to a partisanship objection: it describes the method, not the institute. Reproduce with `intensity_premium` in `scripts/atlas-072026-audit.py`.
- Ad platforms optimize delivery by estimated action rate and let advertisers build audiences from people who engaged with the page. That is enough to explain how a militant group raises its own odds of receiving a pollster's recruitment ad — no coordination needed. Keep the documented mechanism strictly separate from any claim that it was done on purpose.
- Source reports without artifacts (no screenshots, no logs) publish only on the `relato`/hypothesis rung, with the absence of evidence stated in the same breath as the claim, and with an explicit sentence clearing any party the report does not implicate. State what document would settle it — for Atlas, the funnel by origin, creative, campaign and hour with the candidate's vote inside each.
- When auditing an inflated number, close on who it actually costs: it buys short-term debate invitations and screen time, but destroys the diagnosis, the alliance timing and the expectation management of the campaign that celebrates it. That framing is sharper than an accusation and cannot be answered with outrage.
- **Social cards têm uma convenção só, desde 04/08/2026.** Todos saem de `python3 scripts/social-cards.py`, que lê um manifesto único no próprio script, escreve a fonte em `docs/assets/og/<slug>.html` e renderiza `docs/img/og/<slug>.png` em 1200×630 com Chrome headless. Para mudar um texto, edite o manifesto e rode de novo (`--only <slug>` regera um card; `--html` só reescreve as fontes). Nunca edite o HTML gerado nem a imagem à mão.
- Toda página pública tem card próprio, e dossiê e thread têm cards distintos: a thread leva a tarja `Thread` e o acento azul. `docs/social.html` é a galeria de conferência de todos eles, com `noindex`, e não precisa de card.
